senses.definition: A small pocket of seawater left in rocks after the tide goes out.
senses.example: A little crab hid under seaweed at the bottom of the tide pool.

senses.definition: The part of the shore covered by water at high tide and exposed at low tide.
senses.example: The highest barnacles in the intertidal zone spend hours in the open air.

senses.definition: The soft, movable parts that a sea star and some related animals use to move or handle food.
senses.example: The sea star gripped a rock with dozens of tube feet.

senses.definition: Getting food by removing tiny living things or other bits from the water as it flows past or through the body.
senses.example: By filter feeding, the mussel gathers food from seawater.

senses.definition: Seaweed and other natural material left on the beach by waves.
senses.example: Tiny beach hoppers jumped out of the beach wrack.

senses.definition: A shore protected from erosion with natural materials such as plants, sand, or oyster reefs.
senses.example: Oysters grew along the living shoreline beside the bay.

senses.definition: An area where water that is not salty soaks or covers the ground often enough to shape what lives there.
senses.example: Water stood in the freshwater wetland long after the field dried.

senses.definition: A kind of moss that grows in wet places and can help build up peat from its old parts.
senses.example: Bright green peat moss grew on top of the soaked peat.

senses.definition: A shallow wetland pool that holds water for part of the year and often lacks permanent fish populations.
senses.example: When the forest warmed up in spring, salamanders moved into the vernal pool.

senses.definition: A shallow spot where running water ripples over rocks or gravel.
senses.example: The stream riffle made a soft rushing sound under the bridge.

senses.definition: A strip of plants between a stream or other waterway and land next to it.
senses.example: The riparian buffer shaded the creek and held the bank together.

senses.definition: A time when water near the top of a lake mixes with water from farther down.
senses.example: Cold autumn weather and wind helped bring on lake turnover.

senses.definition: The layer made by the highest branches and leaves in a forest.
senses.example: The hawk landed above the forest canopy.

senses.definition: A fallen tree that gives new plants a place to grow as its wood breaks down.
senses.example: Three young trees grew in a row on the old nurse log.

senses.definition: A dead tree that still stands in the woods.
senses.example: The woodpecker built its nest in a hole in a forest snag.

senses.definition: A forest that has grown long enough to develop features such as large old trees and wood that has slowly built up on the ground.
senses.example: Fallen logs and very large trees were both common in the old growth forest.

senses.definition: A forest in a mild or cool region that gets very large amounts of rain or other moisture.
senses.example: Moss covered both the trunks and the ground in the temperate rain forest.

senses.definition: A warm, very wet forest that grows in the tropics.
senses.example: The tall trees in the tropical rain forest stayed green through the year.

senses.definition: The broad band of forests in northern parts of the world, where winters are long and cold.
senses.example: Spruce and fir grew close together in the boreal forest.

senses.definition: The place where a forest meets an open area or a different kind of land.
senses.example: Wild berry bushes grew in bright light by the forest edge.

senses.definition: A change over time in the kinds of living things in a place.
senses.example: Grasses grew first and young trees grew later during ecological succession in the old field.

senses.definition: A wide area with mostly grass in a region with warm and cold seasons.
senses.example: People can find temperate grassland in the middle of North America.

senses.definition: A weather pattern that brings very little rain or snow over a long time.
senses.example: The desert climate was dry even when snow fell in winter.

senses.definition: Land in the far north where the weather is cold and mostly low plants can grow.
senses.example: A thin layer of soil thawed in summer on the arctic tundra.

senses.definition: A layer of ground that stays at or below the freezing point of water for at least two years in a row.
senses.example: Small plants grew only in the soil above the permafrost layer.

senses.definition: The upper boundary on a mountain beyond which forests do not grow.
senses.example: Our path crossed the alpine treeline and the land ahead was open and windy.

senses.definition: A path that shows how food and energy pass from one kind of living thing to the next as it eats the one before it.
senses.example: Grass, a rabbit and a fox can make one food chain.

senses.definition: Dead leaves and other small pieces of plants that collect on top of the soil.
senses.example: The leaf litter under the trees slowly broke into little pieces.

senses.definition: A kind of living thing that has an especially large effect on the other living things around it.
senses.example: A sea star can be a keystone species when it keeps mussels from taking up most of the space on a shore.

senses.definition: A living thing that changes the shape or physical conditions of a place used by other living things.
senses.example: A beaver is an ecosystem engineer when its dam creates a pond.

senses.definition: The breaking of one large natural home into smaller pieces separated by roads, buildings, or other barriers.
senses.example: The new roads caused habitat fragmentation where one forest once stood.

senses.definition: A part of a city that is warmer than nearby areas with fewer streets or buildings and more plants.
senses.example: Our street had a stronger urban heat island before the new trees grew.

senses.definition: A building roof made to support growing plants.
senses.example: The school’s green roof caught some of the rain during the shower.

senses.definition: A plant that occurs naturally in a particular area without having been brought there by people.
senses.example: We chose a native plant that local butterflies can use.

senses.definition: Regular travel by birds between areas where they live at different times of year.
senses.example: In fall, bird migration brings flocks past our town.

senses.definition: A living thing that makes its own food and provides a first source of food for other things in a food chain.
senses.example: The grass in a meadow is a primary producer that can feed grasshoppers and rabbits.

senses.definition: An event in which people search a place for as many kinds of living things as they can find in a short time.
senses.example: During the park bioblitz, Nina made a list of the birds she saw.
